28	
29	\paragraph{Equivalence testing.}
30	We apply a two one-sided $t$-test (TOST) with a $\pm$2\% relative margin (equivalence bounds $\pm$0.047 on the ppl scale) to formally assess whether the depth-aware and random subsampling conditions produce practically indistinguishable perplexity.

Can depth-aware data curation improve downstream language model quality?
We fine-tune OLMo-2-0425-1B on five data variants (3 seeds each) and evaluate perplexity on a held-out test set (Table~\ref{tab:downstream}).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lrc}
\toprule
\textbf{Variant} & \textbf{$n$} & \textbf{Test PPL} \\
\midrule
All depths            & 12{,}299 & 2.335 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Size-matched (random) & 3{,}951  & 2.367 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Depth 0--1 only       & 3{,}951  & 2.387 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
Binary-filtered       & 3{,}951  & 2.389 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
Depth 0 only          & 797      & 2.681 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Downstream fine-tuning perplexity (OLMo-2-0425-1B, mean $\pm$ std across 3 seeds). At equal sample count, random subsampling (2.367) outperforms depth-aware curation (depth 0--1: 2.387, binary-filtered: 2.389).}
\label{tab:downstream}
\end{table}

The results are unambiguous: data quantity dominates depth composition.
Training on all 12{,}299 samples yields the lowest perplexity (2.335).
At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951), random subsampling (2.367) \emph{outperforms} both depth-stratified selection (depth 0--1: 2.387) and binary detection filtering (2.389).
Cross-seed variance is below 0.002 across all variants, which confirms the robustness of this null result.

Restricting training to human-only text (depth 0, $n$\,=\,797) produces a sharp perplexity increase to 2.681, driven primarily by the 5$\times$ reduction in data volume rather than depth composition per se.

\paragraph{Equivalence testing.}
We apply a two one-sided $t$-test (TOST) with a $\pm$2\% relative margin (equivalence bounds $\pm$0.047 on the ppl scale) to formally assess whether the depth-aware and random subsampling conditions produce practically indistinguishable perplexity.
At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951): size-matched (random) ppl\,=\,2.367 vs.\ depth 0--1 ppl\,=\,2.387, $\Delta$\,=\,0.020.
TOST confirms equivalence ($p = 1.1 \times 10^{-4}$); the two curation strategies yield practically indistinguishable downstream quality within the $\pm$2\% margin.
Cross-seed standard deviation is below 0.001 for both variants.

Comparing the full dataset ($n$\,=\,12{,}299, ppl\,=\,2.335) against the depth-filtered subset ($n$\,=\,3{,}951, ppl\,=\,2.387): TOST \emph{rejects} equivalence (minimum equivalence margin\,=\,0.053, exceeding the $\pm$2\% bound), which confirms that data quantity drives perplexity reduction beyond what depth-aware selection can recover.

Knowing the generation depth of a document does not, by itself, make it more or less useful for training; at fixed sample count, depth-aware curation is statistically equivalent to uninformed random subsampling.

\subsection*{Margin Sensitivity Analysis}

To assess the robustness of the equivalence conclusion to margin choice, we repeat the TOST procedure across multiple equivalence margins \cite{lakens_equivalence}, following the recommendation to report sensitivity across plausible bounds rather than relying on a single threshold (Table~\ref{tab:tost-margins}).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Comparison} & \textbf{Margin} & \textbf{Equiv?} & \textbf{TOST $p$} \\
\midrule
Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Random (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                        & $\pm$2\% & Yes & $1 \times 10^{-6}$ \\
                                        & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
                                        & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
\midrule
Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Depth 0--1 (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                            & $\pm$2\% & No & 1.0 \\
                                            & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
                                            & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\caption{TOST equivalence testing across multiple margins. ``Equiv?'' indicates whether equivalence is established at $\alpha = 0.05$.}
\label{tab:tost-margins}
\end{table}

The full dataset vs.\ random subsample comparison passes equivalence at the $\pm$2\% margin ($p = 10^{-6}$), while the full vs.\ depth 0--1 comparison requires a $\pm$3\% margin.
In absolute terms, perplexity differences are small: $\Delta$\,=\,0.032 (full vs.\ random, 1.4\% of baseline) and $\Delta$\,=\,0.052 (full vs.\ depth 0--1, 2.2\% of baseline).

Cohen's $d$ values are 86.0 (full vs.\ random) and 119.7 (full vs.\ depth 0--1).
These appear large but are unreliable: with only $n$\,=\,3 seeds per condition, the pooled standard deviation is extremely small ($<$0.001), artificially inflating $d$.
The inflated effect sizes reflect low seed-level variance (confirming reproducibility) rather than practically meaningful perplexity differences.
The TOST framework with pre-specified relative margins provides a more appropriate assessment than Cohen's $d$ in this low-seed regime.

We complement the permutation importance analysis (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}) with a leave-one-feature-out ablation. Each row drops one of the seven features and re-evaluates the full 6-gen LOGO protocol; $\Delta$ is the change relative to the full 7-feature ensemble (F1\,=\,0.789).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Dropped feature} & \textbf{LOGO F1} & $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ \textbf{vs Full} \\
\midrule
entropy\_max    & 0.774 & $-$1.50\,pp \\
entropy\_mean   & 0.783 & $-$0.63\,pp \\
ttr             & 0.784 & $-$0.55\,pp \\
hapax\_ratio    & 0.785 & $-$0.42\,pp \\
tail\_decay     & 0.786 & $-$0.33\,pp \\
entropy\_std    & 0.786 & $-$0.29\,pp \\
entropy\_min    & 0.789 & $+$0.01\,pp \\
\midrule
Full (7 features) & 0.789 & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Leave-one-feature-out ablation (6-gen LOGO). Each row drops one feature and re-evaluates with the LOGO protocol. Sorted by impact magnitude.}
\label{tab:lofo}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Analysis.}
Entropy\_max causes the largest degradation when removed ($-$1.5\,pp), despite ranking only fourth in permutation importance (split frequency 0.063). This indicates that entropy\_max provides unique signal (capturing the most surprising token under the reference model) that is not redundant with other features.
Conversely, entropy\_min is fully redundant ($\Delta$\,=\,+0.01\,pp), consistent with its near-zero permutation importance (0.015).
Six of seven features contribute positively to the ensemble, which confirms that the 7-feature design is not over-specified.

content.thinking:
Now I have all the information needed to respond to Reviewer 1's points. Let me go through each one:

### Must-Fix

**N1**: DDR 三分阈值为 post-hoc 选择
- R1 says: thresholds |ρ|>0.60 and |ρ|<0.10 are post-hoc, 6x gap, sensitivity ±0.10 only shows local stability, circular logic risk
- My assessment: I agree with this. The paper's §4.2 line 68 states "shifting thresholds by ±0.10 does not alter grouping" but this is indeed a very narrow sensitivity check. 

The thresholds look like they were selected after examining the data, with no prior theoretical basis provided. The 3/1/3 split seems too convenient, and R1's recommendations for holdout validation or data-driven clustering approaches make sense here.
- Verdict: [AGREE]

**N2**: Near-stationary 标签不稳健：TOST 仅 4/8 generator 通过 tail_decay
- R1 says: tail_decay passes TOST only 4/8 generators
- My verification: From Appendix T (Table), tail_decay passes for: Pythia-2.8B (0.07✓), Pythia-1B (0.08

✓), Qwen3-1.7B (0.09✓), Qwen3-0.6B (0.08✓). It fails for: Llama-3.2-3B (0.19), OLMo-2-1B (0.22), Qwen3-8B (0.15), Mistral-7B (0.16). So 4/8 is correct.
- The paper acknowledges this in §4.2 line 76: "Tail decay's mixed TOST results (|d| up to 0.22) place it at the boundary of the near-stationary group."
- R1 is right that 4/8 generators passing is weak support for classifying tail_decay as near-stationary, though the paper does acknowledge the mixed results and relies on the pooled effect size of 0.08 to justify the classification.

The pooled statistic obscures the fact that half the generators actually show meaningful differences. R1's meta-analytic TOST suggestion might be overly technical, but the core issue stands—calling something near-stationary when it fails on half the models is misleading. I agree with this critique, though it's more of a labeling problem than a fundamental error.

For the feature redundancy point, R1 correctly identifies that TTR and hapax are nearly perfectly correlated at r=0.97, and entropy_min contributes almost nothing to the model with a LOFO change of just 0.01 percentage points. I've verified both claims in the appendix and the paper's results section. The DDR structure is indeed weaker than presented because of this redundancy.

I do agree the redundancy is a real issue, but I'd push back slightly on removing entropy_min entirely—the paper already acknowledges the feature adds negligible value, which is an honest characterization. The bigger problem is that DDR should be described more accurately as roughly 2 independent drifting signals, 1 intermediate, and 2-3 near-stationary components rather than the cleaner 3/1/3 breakdown the paper suggests.

On the temperature sensitivity point, the Abstract and Introduction do mention base models as a limitation but completely gloss over the fact that results only hold when temperature is kept at 0.7 or below. That's a significant constraint that deserves explicit mention upfront.

For the generator subsets, the explanation does exist in §3.4, but it's buried and doesn't stand out enough. Readers see different subset sizes scattered across tables and appendices without a clear, centralized reference, which creates unnecessary confusion even though the information is technically there.

On the downstream TOST analysis, I'm checking the seed count in Appendix L—it looks like only 3 seeds were used per condition, and the effect sizes are quite large (Cohen's d around 86 and 120).  The paper acknowledges these are unreliable due to the tiny pooled standard deviation, yet still argues TOST is more appropriate than Cohen's d in this regime. But TOST itself requires adequate sample sizes to be trustworthy, so this doesn't resolve the underlying issue.

The cross-domain experiments introduce a temperature confound—the main Wikipedia work uses t=0.7 while the cross-domain evaluation switches to t=1.0. The appendix even notes this discrepancy, acknowledging that different temperatures favor different experimental conditions. That's a clear confound that weakens the comparison.

For the equivalence bound, the paper sets ε=0.20 based on Cohen's conventional "small effect" threshold from behavioral sciences, but doesn't justify why this particular boundary makes sense for characterizing "near-stationary" behavior in NLL distributions across recursive generation. It's borrowed from a different domain without domain-specific grounding.

On the missing references claim—I'm checking whether Lakens is actually cited. Looking at Appendix T, the TOST procedure does cite Lakens, so that criticism doesn't hold up.

The ordinal classification literature coverage seems reasonable for a paper that uses ordinal framing without making methodological contributions—they cite the main surveys and methods. Could be more comprehensive, but it's not a glaring gap.

For the specific questions raised: the DDR threshold analysis is addressed in the appendix, the entropy/TTR ablation is covered, the model-dependent temperature split between Qwen and the other models is noted but not explained, and the downstream evaluation with multiple seeds is also documented.

Now I'm drafting the cross-review response.

## Reviewer 2 — 交叉回应 Reviewer 1 Round 1

---

### Must-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R1-N1: DDR 三分阈值为 post-hoc 选择，缺乏先验依据**

同意 R1 的核心判断。§4.2 第 68 行的 sensitivity analysis（"shifting thresholds by ±0.10 does not alter grouping"）确实只证明了局部稳定性，无法排除 post-hoc overfitting 风险。补充两个我的观察：

1. 论文的 DDR 分组实际依赖四个统计量的"convergence"（ρ, d, Levene, CV shift; §4.2 第 74 行），但没有形式化定义什么构成"convergence"——每个统计量的阈值都是隐式的。
2. Figure (Appendix T) 的 DDR scatter plot 虽然视觉上显示三组间有 gap，但视觉 gap ≠ 统计显著分组。R1 建议的 holdout generator 验证或 data-driven clustering（如 k-means on (|ρ|, d) space）是必要的。

**[AGREE] R1-N2: Near-stationary 标签不稳健——tail_decay TOST 仅 4/8 通过**

同意。我已在 Appendix T Table 中逐行验证：tail_decay 通过等价性的仅 Pythia-2.8B (d=0.07), Pythia-1B (0.08), Qwen3-1.7B (0.09), Qwen3-0.6B (0.08)。未通过的四个 generator 中，OLMo-2-1B 的 |d|=0.22 已超出 ε=0.20。论文在 §4.2 第 76 行承认 "mixed TOST results" 但仍坚持 near-stationary 分类，理由是 pooled d=0.08 和 CV<3%。

我的补充判断：pooled statistic 在此场景下 masks generator-level heterogeneity。如果 tail_decay 在半数 generator 上表现为 non-stationary，将其 pooled 后标注为 near-stationary 是 Simpson's paradox 风险。R1 建议 random-effects meta-analytic TOST 有些过度规定方法，但核心要求（tail_decay 应重新归类或标注为 borderline）合理。

不过补充一个 nuance：即使 tail_decay 重新归类为 borderline/intermediate，DDR 仍保留 "entropy_min (8/8) + entropy_max (6/8)" 两个较稳健的 near-stationary 特征，所以 DDR 结构不会完全瓦解——但确实从 clean 3/1/3 退化为更 messy 的分组。

**[AGREE] R1-N3: 特征冗余严重削弱 DDR 结构的信息独立性**

完全同意。这与我自己的 W4 (TTR/hapax r=0.97 问题) 一致。逐条确认：

1. TTR/hapax r=0.97——论文 §3.3 第 69 行、§4.2 第 81 行均确认。两个特征本质上是同一信号，DDR 的 "3 drifting" 实际只有 2 个独立 drifting signal（entropy_mean + lexical diversity）。
2. entropy_min LOFO ΔF1=+0.01pp——Appendix H (LOFO Table) 确认。移除后性能不变甚至微升，表明其对分类零贡献。
3. R1 的结论 "DDR 实际为 ~2/1/~2" 是准确的。

我进一步补充：即使保留全部 7 个特征用于分类（因为冗余不影响 XGBoost 性能），DDR 的 **结构性 claim** 应修正为 "2 independent drifting signals / 1 intermediate / 2 consistently near-stationary + 1 borderline (tail_decay)"。这比 3/1/3 更诚实，但 novelty 也更弱。

---

### Should-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R1-W1: 温度限定未在 Abstract/Introduction 中说明**

同意。Abstract（abstract.tex 第 5 行）未提及 t≤0.7 这一关键操作条件。§4.2 显示 t=0.9 时 binary F1 下降 9.3-26.0pp，这是该方法能否成立的边界条件，应在 Abstract 中前置。

**[AGREE] R1-W2: Generator subset 不一致，缺乏集中说明**

部分同意。§3.4 第 75 行确实有一段集中解释（"three overlapping generator subsets reflecting chronological expansion"），因此 R1 说"缺乏集中说明"不完全准确。但该说明不够显著，读者在阅读不同 appendix tables 时仍容易困惑于 5-gen/6-gen/8-gen 的切换。建议将此说明提升为独立 paragraph 或加 Table 汇总 subset 定义。

**[AGREE] R1-W3: 下游效用 TOST 统计基础薄弱（n=3 seeds）**

同意。Appendix L 使用 n=3 seeds，Cohen's d 被 inflated 至 86.0 和 119.7（论文自承 "unreliable"，Appendix L 第 70 行）。TOST 在 n=3 下的 statistical power 极低，等价性结论不可靠。这也与我的 N2 (downstream utility 为负但论证薄弱) 一致。

**[AGREE] R1-W4: 跨域实验存在温度 confound**

同意。appendix_domain.tex 第 25 行自承 main experiment 用 t=0.7，cross-domain 用 t=1.0，且存在 "domain × temperature interaction"。跨域实验的结论因此被 temperature confound 污染，无法区分 domain transfer 和 temperature effect。

**[AGREE] R1-W5: TOST ε=0.20 缺乏领域特定论证**

同意。ε=0.20 (Cohen's d) 是 behavioral science 的惯例阈值（Cohen 1988 "small effect"），但论文未论证该阈值在 NLL distribution 特征的递归生成场景下为何合适。不同 ε 值会直接改变 near-stationary group 的成员构成——如果 ε=0.15，entropy_max 也会有 2/8 generator 未通过 (Pythia-1B d=0.21, Pythia-2.8B d=0.25)；如果 ε=0.25，tail_decay 会多通过几个 generator。阈值选择本身也是 post-hoc 的。

---

### Missing References

**[REBUT] R1-MR1: Lakens (2017) TOST 方法论缺失**

R1 声称缺少 Lakens (2017) 引用，但这一判断不正确。论文已在两处引用 Lakens：
- Appendix T (TOST equivalence testing) 第 4 行: `\cite{lakens_equivalence}`
- Appendix L (downstream TOST) 第 41 行: `\cite{lakens_equivalence}`

grep 确认 `lakens` 在 appendix_tost.tex 和 appendix_downstream.tex 中各出现一次。R1 可能未仔细检查附录引用。

**[AGREE] R1-MR2: 更多 ordinal classification 文献**

部分同意。论文已引用 gutierrez_ordinal_survey, coral_ordinal, corn_ordinal, frank_hall_ordinal 四篇 ordinal classification 文献（§2.1, §3.4），对于一篇将 ordinal classification 作为 framing 而非方法论贡献的论文来说覆盖度尚可，但若论文要强调 "ordinal classification" 作为 task formulation 的新颖性，则应讨论更多该领域的 methodology 及其与 depth classification 的适配性。

---

### Questions 回应

**[AGREE] R1-Q1: DDR 阈值是事前还是事后？**
有效问题，已在 N1 中讨论。论文未给出先验依据。

**[AGREE] R1-Q2: 移除 entropy_min 并合并 TTR/hapax 后 DDR 是否成立？**
关键问题。如果 DDR 在 effective ~5 features 上变为 ~2/1/~2，"tri-partition" 的 narrative 需要调整。作者应提供该消融实验。

**[AGREE] R1-Q3: Model-dependent 温度响应原因？**
有效问题。§4.2 第 87 行描述了 Pythia/OLMo vs. Qwen 的分裂但仅归因于 "model-family differences"，未给出 mechanistic explanation。论文也提到可能与 tokenizer 差异有关（Limitations 第 29 行），但未验证。

**[AGREE] R1-Q4: Downstream n=10+ seeds 结论是否改变？**
已在 W3 中讨论。n=3 seeds 的 TOST 统计 power 不足，需更多 seeds 才能确认 null result。

**[AGREE] R1-Q5: 跨域实验生成温度？**
已在 W4 中讨论。Temperature confound 使跨域结论不可靠。

---

### 综合判断

R1 的 3 个 Must-Fix 问题均有数据支撑，其中 N2 (tail_decay TOST 4/8) 和 N3 (特征冗余) 是可直接用论文自身数据验证的 factual 判断。N1 (post-hoc 阈值) 是方法论质疑，合理但难以决定性地证伪。5 个 Should-Fix 均为有效观察。Missing References 中 Lakens 的指控不成立（论文已引用）。

R1 给出 Overall 3.0 (Findings) 比我的 2.5 (Borderline Findings) 高 0.5 分。差异主要在于：
1. R1 侧重 methodological rigor（DDR 分组的统计稳健性），而我同时考虑了 novelty/impact（方法论零创新、downstream 为负、instruct 不可用）。
2. R1 的 Must-Fix 问题本质上是 "DDR 的证据不够强"，而我的 Must-Fix 还包括 "即使 DDR 成立，贡献也不足以发表"。
3. R1 的评分假设 DDR 证据修补后论文可接受；我认为即使统计问题全部修复，novelty 和 practical impact 仍不足以达到 Findings 标准。

**建议 Overall: 维持 2.5 (Borderline Findings)**，即使考虑 R1 相对宽松的评分，综合两人意见应在 2.5-3.0 区间。
